actions.description: Advance the simulated world by a bounded number of fixed timesteps, optionally applying an action for each step, and return the resulting observation and terminal flags.

inputs.description: Transitions to advance; the action is applied at every tick
inputs.name: ticks

inputs.description: The action applied at each tick, shaped by the environment's action space
inputs.name: action

actions.name: step

actions.description: Reset the simulated world to a scenario start state and return the initial observation. When a seed is supplied the endpoint records it in the receipt; otherwise the endpoint's declared default seed applies.

inputs.description: Accepted for the class contract; a MuJoCo reset restores the model defaults (mj_resetData) and does not use a seed
inputs.name: seed

actions.name: reset

facts.text: The README's sim-to-sim procedure tells the user to update the policy_config in sim2sim/configs/n2_18dof.yaml before starting the MuJoCo deployment
The README labels the deployment MuJoCo-based sim-to-sim and gives python sim2sim/sim2sim.py as the command
The sim2sim config selects resources/robots/N2/mjcf/n2_18dof.xml as the model
The sim2sim config sets simulation_dt to 0.002 s and control_decimation to 10
run_mujoco opens the YAML config named by its cfg argument and resolves its xml_path
run_mujoco loads the robot model with mujoco.MjModel.from_xml_path(xml_path)
run_mujoco overwrites model.opt.timestep with the config's simulation_dt and then creates MjData
run_mujoco computes PD torques and writes the torque vector to data.ctrl
run_mujoco advances the simulation with mujoco.mj_step(model, data)
The script's __main__ block defaults the config file to n2_10dof.yaml
The MJCF root element declares the model N2
The model uses radians and resolves its meshes from ../meshes/
The default joint class sets damping 0.001, armature 0.01 and frictionloss 0.1
The base_link body is placed at 0 0 0.75 and carries the free joint named root
Eighteen limited hinge joints carry the arms and legs: four per arm and five per leg, each with its own range
The actuator section declares eighteen motor actuators, one per hinge joint
No actuator element sets ctrlrange or ctrllimited, so the model states no control range for any motor
The package declares mujoco==2.3.6 and mujoco-python-viewer in install_requires
The package declares isaacgym (preview 4) in install_requires

determinism.notes: MuJoCo integrates a fixed model deterministically from the model defaults; cap.world.reset.v1 restores those defaults and the bridge's seed input is accepted for the class contract but a MuJoCo reset does not use it.  The package's stand-in is deterministic too, but its placeholder motion is not the engine's physics.

gaps: the fake backend is a stand-in for the mujoco library, not MuJoCo: it parses the MJCF for the free base, the eighteen hinge joints, the eighteen motor actuators and the option time step, then gives each actuated hinge a placeholder velocity proportional to its control value and holds the free base where the model puts it; it computes no inertia, torque, gravity, contact, friction, constraint, damping or actuator dynamics and produces no MuJoCo trajectory
the stand-in loads no STL mesh or texture and resolves no collision or contact, so the model's floor, base collision geoms and armature attributes are not applied

the model's sensor section and sites (foot forces, IMU) are not read or exposed; the upstream loop reads the two foot-force sensors (sim2sim.py:148-155), but this package serves only the bridge's integration state

the model declares no ctrlrange or ctrllimited for its motors, so the bridge publishes action.ctrl operator_required: a step that sets it is refused until the site's site-limits.json bounds it, and site-limits.example.json is operator example data, not a model bound; the upstream sim2sim loop clips no torque either and writes the PD result to data.ctrl

the model states no <option timestep>, so the stand-in uses the 2 ms MuJoCo library default; the upstream sim2sim loop overwrites the model step with its config's 0.002 s (n2_18dof.yaml:8, sim2sim.py:91), which is this package's published timestep
the upstream sim2sim loop drives the model with a TorchScript policy and a keyboard command object; this package serves the model alone and takes the control vector from the caller
MuJoCo itself was not importable where the gate ran, so no trajectory of this package was compared with the real engine
snapshot and restore fall back to copying time, qpos, qvel and ctrl because the stand-in implements no mj_getState/mj_setState, so a restore is not exact
no physical humanoid is modelled and nothing was validated against the N2 hardware

measures.description: Simulated time since the last reset
measures.name: time_ms

measures.description: Control vector last applied to the actuators (ctrl)
measures.name: ctrl

measures.description: Integration steps since the last reset
measures.name: tick

measures.description: Integration step of the model (null when the model states none)
measures.name: timestep_ms

measures.description: Seed the bridge was configured with
measures.name: seed

measures.description: Declared native checkpoint. Integration profile restores the full native input vector; basic profile restores only advertised state plus actuator activation and exact native time. Neither profile certifies external callbacks, plugins, RNG or hardware fidelity.
measures.name: native_checkpoint

operator_required.name: step
operator_required.reason: the model gives none of its actuators no control range (ctrllimited false or no ctrlrange), so MuJoCo leaves the control unclamped; site-limits.json must bound action.ctrl before a step can set it

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the integration state is kept and stays readable
